messages:
Maya - People Ops: Quick heads-up: two small but important PTO/ travel policy items rolling out next quarter :wave:
Maya - People Ops: 1) Carryover Buffer pilot — starting 2026-06-01 we’ll let people carry over up to 5 unused PTO hours beyond the normal cap for a single 6-month grace window. The idea: reduce pressure to use partial days right before year-end. This is a pilot for 6 months and applies to full-time employees globally.
Maya - People Ops: 2) Travel conduct reminder + emergency reimbursement tweak — we clarified expectations for reimbursing same-day emergency travel during company-sponsored work (see link). For international trips, receipts still required but we’ll accept digital attestations for last-minute bookings when receipts can’t be obtained immediately.
andrew-eng: Thanks — for the carryover buffer, does this stack with manager-approved PTO advance?
Maya - People Ops: Good q. No stacking with PTO advance. The buffer is meant for small leftover hours only (<=5 hours); if you have an advance open that reduces your accruals, normal advance rules apply.
Jess (People Ops): Adding: managers will see the buffer in People Portal; it’s an automated flag, no manual forms needed.
marta-people-sr: Is this retroactive to accruals from previous year? I had 8 hours leftover from last year.
Maya - People Ops: Not retroactive — pilot starts 2026-06-01 so only hours accrued after that date are eligible. If the pilot goes well we’ll discuss broader changes.
sre_oncall: Travel reimbursement tweak — does this change per-diem rules for overnight on-call rotations where someone has to fly home?
Maya - People Ops: Short answer: no change to per-diem. Longer: emergency one-way flights home for documented family emergencies can be reimbursed under the existing emergency travel policy; the tweak only relaxes receipt submission timing for certain international carriers.
andrew-eng: Any changes to blackout windows or team coverage expectations? We have a product launch in July.
Maya - People Ops: No new blackout windows in this announcement. Teams can still set local coverage windows (as usual) — we encourage teams to post them in shared calendars. If you need a formal exception for leave during an active launch, talk to your manager and ping People Ops; we’ll handle escalations.
people-ops-bot: Policy update posted: https://intranet.redwood.com/policies/carryover-buffer-pilot (doc updated by Maya - People Ops) :memo:
Jess (People Ops): TL;DR: carryover buffer = small safety net (<=5h), pilot runs 6 months; travel receipts can be attested digitally in narrow emergency cases; no stacking with PTO advance; not retroactive.
marta-people-sr: Thanks, noted. Will share with my team and add a calendar reminder.
Maya - People Ops: Thanks all — open to feedback during the pilot. If you spot edge cases, DM me or drop a note in #people-ops. :sparkles:
